title: Pointers: The Basics
description: Understand memory addresses and pointers. Learn how to reference and dereference values, and why pointers are essential for systems programming.
objectives: Understand what pointers are and why they're useful
Pass values by reference to functions

sections.title: What are Pointers?
sections.content:
A **pointer** is a variable that stores a **memory address**.

```
Variable:  local x: int = 42;
Memory:    [  42  ]  ← stored at address 0x1000
           
Pointer:   local p: *int = &x;
           [0x1000]  ← stores the ADDRESS of x
```

**Why use pointers?**
- **Efficiency**: Pass large data without copying
- **Mutability**: Modify variables in calling code
- **Dynamic memory**: Allocate memory at runtime
- **Data structures**: Build linked lists, trees, graphs

sections.title: Pointer Syntax Comparison
sections.explanation: BPL uses *Type for pointer type, & for address-of, and * for dereference - same as C.

sections.title: Creating and Using Pointers
sections.expectedOutput:
x = 42
Address of x: 0x...
Value at ptr (*ptr): 42

After *ptr = 100:
x = 100
*ptr = 100

After x = 999:

lineExplanations.7: &x gets the memory address of x.
lineExplanations.13: *ptr dereferences - gets value at that address.

sections.title: Pass by Reference
sections.expectedOutput:

Calling tryToDouble...
Inside tryToDouble: 20
After tryToDouble: 10

Calling actuallyDouble...
Inside actuallyDouble: 20
After actuallyDouble: 20

lineExplanations.4: Parameter is copied - changes don't affect original.
lineExplanations.11: *n dereferences to read and write the original variable.

sections.expectedOutput:

After swap: x=20, y=10
After second swap: x=10, y=20

lineExplanations.5: Save *a (value at address a) to temp.
lineExplanations.6: Put value from b into a.
lineExplanations.7: Put original value of a (temp) into b.

sections.title: Pointers to Structs
sections.expectedOutput:
Initial: Point(0, 0)
After move(5, 10): Point(5, 10)
After move(-3, 7): Point(2, 17)

lineExplanations.8: *Point is a pointer to a Point struct.
lineExplanations.10: BPL allows p.x instead of (*p).x for convenience.
lineExplanations.22: &point passes the address of the struct.

sections.title: Multiple Pointers, Same Data

lineExplanations.17: Changing through one pointer affects all.
lineExplanations.7-9: All three pointers point to the same memory.
lineExplanations.21-22: All pointers see the new value.

sections.title: Pointer Dangers ⚠️
sections.content:
Pointers are powerful but dangerous:

**Null Pointer Dereference**
```bpl
local p: *int = nullptr;
*p = 10;  # CRASH! Can't write to null
```

**Dangling Pointer** (pointing to freed memory)
```bpl
local p: *int = allocate();  # Get memory
free(p);                     # Free it
*p = 10;  # BAD! Memory is gone
```

**Uninitialized Pointer**
```bpl
local p: *int;  # Points to... somewhere random?
*p = 10;        # Writing to random memory!
```

**Always initialize pointers** and **check for null** before dereferencing!

sections.expectedOutput:

lineExplanations.5: Always check for nullptr before dereferencing.
lineExplanations.24: nullptr is the safe 'no value' for pointers.

sections.title: Practice: Array Statistics with Pointers
sections.instructions:
Write a function `stats(arr: *int, len: int, outMin: *int, outMax: *int, outSum: *int)` that:
1. Calculates min, max, and sum of an array
2. Writes results to the output pointers

Test with array [5, 2, 8, 1, 9]
sections.hint: Initialize min/max to the first element, then loop through the rest.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
sections.content:
✅ **Pointer** stores a memory address, not a value

✅ **&variable** gets the address of a variable

✅ ***pointer** dereferences - accesses the value at the address

✅ **Pass by pointer** allows functions to modify caller's variables

✅ ***Type** is the type of a pointer to Type

✅ **nullptr** represents a null (invalid) pointer

✅ **Always check for null** before dereferencing!

questions.question: What does the & operator do?
options: Gets the address of a variable
questions.explanation: & is the address-of operator. It returns the memory address of a variable.

questions.question: What does the * operator do when used with a pointer?
questions.explanation: * dereferences a pointer, giving you the value stored at that memory address.

questions.question: Why would you pass a pointer to a function?
options: To let the function modify the original variable
questions.explanation: Passing a pointer allows the function to access and modify the original variable.
